correctness.rationale: Direct Gaussian integration gives W=e^(−q²−p²)[e^(−a²)cosh(2aq)+cos(2ap)]/[π(1+e^(−a²))]; the integrated negative part has no further factor of two. Set β=acos(e^(−a²)) and t=(π−β)/(2a). Negative points have bounded position and lie in the stated momentum intervals; at q=0 a negative open region starts immediately to the right of t for every a>0. Lobes beyond the nearest symmetric pair start at |p|≥t+π/a and their total Gaussian tail is exponentially smaller. An alternative scaling p=t+as, q=√a w gives negative bracket divided by a³ tending to 2√2 s−2w² and exponential ratio tending to e^(−πs), with Jacobian a^(3/2). The exact identity for the cosine difference gives a bound C a³s, and the cosh lower bound restricts w²≤Cs; the integrand is dominated by C s e^(−cs) on that support. Integrating the parabolic positive part against e^(−πs), normalizing and accounting for both lobes gives (2^(7/4)/π³) a^(9/2)e^(−t²). The edge expansion t=π/(2a)−1/√2+O(a²) contributes both the positive 1/a exponent and e^(−1/2). Independent scaled Simpson quadrature for the nearest pair (s truncated at 17, 2048 panels, 64 position panels) gave ratios to the stated equivalent near 0.96317, 0.98295, 0.99351, 0.99681 at a=0.10,0.05,0.02,0.01; these corroborate, but do not establish, the analytic limit. The frozen checks/check_cat.py and its recorded results were inspected, not executed.
